result.instructions: Tools to build real-time strategy games with AIVERSE: a game is data (game.json, rules.json, maps). STRATA virtual geometry: strata_capabilities reports compiled authoring support; strata_model_analyze {model: project-relative path} builds read-only CPU staging, not GPU acceptance. Projects live anywhere on disk; the engine ships templates (sample games). Workflow: list_projects (recent projects + templates) / create_project {name, template, location} / open_game {game: folder} -> read rules_schema (the data format reference) -> rules_list / rules_get -> edit rules with rules_set / rules_merge (keep rules small: shared values in an "abstract": true base that entries "extends", levels only with what changes; big games split rules.json with "include": ["rules/units.json", ...], the rules ops save each entry back to its file; docs/game-format.md 'Splitting rules.json') -> build maps (map_new, terrain_paint, terrain_level, field_paint, region_paint, entity_place, player_set, map_set for waves/triggers/areas/victory) -> map_validate -> match_run (bots, balance check) -> map_save {addToGame:true} -> view_screenshot to look at it -> build_start for a platform. map_ascii gives a quick text picture of a map. 2D tile games: tileset_list, tiles_init, tile_paint. Dungeon / territory games: terrain_paint with the game's map characters, territory_paint. Relief: terrain_sculpt (sub-cell detail, erode, stamp), terrain_detail, terrain_paint_material, terrain_heights, terrain_material, heightmap_import / heightmap_export. Other data files (lang/*.json, audio.json, tilesets, fx, ui/*.rml): game_file_read / game_file_write; models, textures, sounds: asset_import. Balancing: balance_stats (numbers side by side: DPS per armor, value per cost) -> balance_duel / balance_matrix (arena fights at equal cost: who counters whom) -> rules_set to adjust -> balance_batch (many bot matches: win rate per slot and faction, match length, what never gets built; 'mirror' separates map side from faction). Online battles (direct-control PvP / PvE): battle_net_simulate {profile: bad, tickRate, rollbackWindow} checks network settings on a simulated mobile link (docs/battle-net.md). Phones: device_list {filter} (iPhone, iPad, Pixel, Galaxy, Redmi, desktops: sizes, safe areas, cut-outs) -> device_set {device, orientation, safeArea: true} -> view_screenshot {window: game}. The game's own screens (main menu, levels, shop, profile, settings, popups; RmlUi + Lua): ui_api -> ui_screen_create {name, template} -> game_file_write ui/screens/<name>.rml -> ui_validate -> ui_preview {screen, device}. To test a mechanic by playing: play_start, play_units, play_command (any player command, e.g. surrender, dig, ability), play_status. Mechanics the data blocks can't express: Lua scripts - script_api (reference) -> script_write {path: scripts/x.lua, register: true} -> script_check (compile + short bot match, errors with file:line); simulation scripts use integers and fx() numbers, no floats. Import projects: port_scan {path}, port_import {path,out,scale?}, port_report, port_item {id}. For missing mechanics use rules_schema, then Lua, then native modules. Verify scenario_run/bot matches and source screenshots; port_resolve {id,how,reason} records verified work. Visual effects: fx_templates (explosion, fire, smoke, magic, weather, ...) or fx_import_unity {source: a Unity .prefab / folder} to make the same effect as a Unity one, tune with fx_get / fx_set, look with fx_preview {effect, advance, freeze} + view_screenshot, attach to events with fx_bind (died, hit, attack, ability, spawned per type / weapon / ability). LENS cameras: lens_scene_get -> lens_scene_validate -> lens_camera_set / lens_scene_set / lens_camera_delete; lens_camera_presets lists camera presets for game.json camera, topDown.camera, camera.chase / firstPerson and a camera's follow block. Writes require expectedRevision (the revision from the last lens_scene_get; expectedScene is still accepted) and save immediately without undo; Reload the native LENS window afterward. Look of the game: own meshes / textures via asset_import, then the type's "view" block with rules_merge (model, materials overrides per material name, team colour, clips: docs/models.md; model_info lists nodes, clips, materials); custom materials: texture_generate (bricks, metal panels, wood, camo, scales, ... + normal maps, team masks) -> material_set (shared library materials.json) -> material_apply {type, material, target | node} -> material_preview + view_screenshot; lighting: lighting_set (sun, sky, day/night, presets), light_add / light_update (point lights on the map); PHYSIS map authoring: physis_get -> physis_validate -> physis_set with expectedRevision from physis_get; these edit map configuration only, not live simulation or visual fog. fog of war: rules_merge {path: "fogOfWar"} (mode, colour, style, softness, grid, lineOfSight for 3D visibility by heights, vision.blocks on wall types, delivery.blocksVision on smoke skills); Scene entities/components: scene_entity_list -> scene_entity_get -> scene_component_set. Lights: scene_light_create/delete with persistent entityId; configure GI/Luma with scene_render_lighting_get/set. Read engine skills/editor/aiverse-scene-entities/SKILL.md and skills/visuals/aiverse-lighting/SKILL.md; map_save persists requested edits. Other legacy scene IDs remain provisional. post effects (bloom, colour grading, LUT, vignette, tilt-shift, ...): postfx_catalog -> postfx_preset / postfx_add; their answers carry 'warnings' with ms per frame for heavy effects (bloom, fxaa, sunShafts) - pass them on to the user; view_postfx {quality: low} + view_screenshot shows what weak phones get; game UI: ui_contract (documents, data bindings, events) -> game_file_write ui/hud.rml, ui/skin.rcss ... (the game's ui/ overrides the engine's). Map edits appear live in the editor with undo. Project-file tools describe their own save and reload behavior. You can only change game projects, never the engine.

tools.name: lens_scene_get
tools.description: Read project cameras.json (missing = empty v1 scene), runtime validation and normalized defaults. Does not render. Returns an opaque revision: pass it as expectedRevision when editing (expectedScene with the returned scene is still accepted).

tools.name: lens_camera_presets
tools.description: List the named camera presets (engine/render/CameraPresets.h): name, body (overhead = game.json camera, follow = topDown.camera / a map camera / a cameras.json camera "follow" block, chase / firstPerson = rules or map camera.chase / camera.firstPerson) and their keys. Pass a name to get one. Use a preset in any of those blocks as {"preset": name, ...overrides}. Read only.

tools.name: lens_scene_validate
tools.description: Validate a v1 camera scene with the native loader, without changing files. normalizedScene exposes defaults/clamping; clientCompatible means texture-only outputs, not GPU acceptance.

tools.name: lens_scene_set
tools.description: Replace cameras.json after native validation. Requires expectedRevision (or expectedScene) from lens_scene_get; a stale one fails without writing. Saves immediately; no editor undo. Reload the LENS window/restart the client to consume it. Does not enable game.json lens.enabled.

tools.name: lens_camera_set
tools.description: Create or replace one complete camera record by positive id, preserving other records. Requires expectedRevision (or expectedScene) from lens_scene_get. For partial edits merge locally first. Saves immediately; Reload LENS afterward.

tools.name: lens_camera_delete
tools.description: Remove one camera record by positive id. Requires expectedRevision (or expectedScene) from lens_scene_get; unknown ids fail without writes. Saves immediately; no undo or live GPU resource deletion.

tools.name: geometry_proxy_bake

tools.name: geometry_proxy_lod
tools.description: Append a baked surface proxy to a rules type's existing view.lod. Requires the expected source model; preserves other view settings and rejects animated sources. Distance is explicit; inspect transitions and material overrides.

tools.name: strata_capabilities
tools.description: Report compiled STRATA authoring support, analysis limits and verification boundaries; not live GPU status.

tools.name: strata_model_analyze

tools.name: geometry_catalog
tools.description: Geometry optimization choices, eligibility and platform-independent budgets. Analyze assets before selecting policies.

tools.name: geometry_analyze
tools.description: Inspect a real model and report eligibility, cluster reduction and a suggested policy. Does not modify the game or claim measured GPU speedup.

tools.name: geometry_policy_set
tools.description: Validate and save a rules type's view.geometry policy. Existing LOD and instancing settings are preserved.

tools.name: geometry_scene_validate

tools.name: geometry_scene_get
tools.description: Read the saved geometry.json static scenery manifest.

tools.name: geometry_scene_set
tools.description: Validate and atomically save geometry.json. Grid maps: applies game-wide static scenery and rebuilds views. World-space maps: set map geometryScene=geometry.json separately. Never move gameplay entities into static scenery.

tools.name: geometry_strata_set
tools.description: Force STRATA, force the LOD path or return to auto for one object (instance id) of the static geometry scene.

tools.name: model_info
tools.description: Inspect a type model without requiring a visible Models window; lists nodes, clips, materials and loader warnings.

tools.name: modeling_volume_texture_import
tools.description: Read a project SPVT density texture frame as a portable volumeCsg densityTexture node.

tools.name: modeling_catalog
tools.description: Authoring operation catalog, format limits and exact algorithm coverage.

tools.description: List project model source assets.

tools.name: modeling_create
tools.description: Create a versioned model source; preset empty or robot, or explicit document. Refuses overwrite.

tools.name: modeling_get

tools.description: Read the shared authoring document with rig, clips, graph and revision.

tools.name: modeling_redo
tools.description: Undo/redo an asset edit. Requires expectedRevision; revisions always increase.

tools.name: modeling_validate
tools.description: Validate geometry, hierarchy, skin weights, clips and compile graph with actual model. No writes.

tools.name: rig_validate
tools.description: Validate geometry, hierarchy, skin weights, clips and compile graph with actual model. No writes.

tools.name: animation_bake

tools.description: Build and report a document. async=true starts a bounded background job; poll modeling_job_status.

tools.name: animation_generate
tools.description: Generate editable motion keys. tracks: node/path/axis/wave(sine,spin,fold,recoil)/amplitude/frequency/phase/offset. Requires expectedRevision.

tools.description: Create and export a separate simplified source asset. Requires expectedRevision, target, cell; preserves node/clip names. Explicit skin weights must be regenerated.

tools.name: modeling_export
tools.description: Export current model to models/<name>.glb with nodes, PBR, skins and clips; requires expectedRevision.

tools.name: modeling_graph_publish
tools.description: Export model and publish a graph snapshot to animations/. Requires expectedRevision; existing graph needs expectedGraph.

tools.name: modeling_graph_import
tools.description: Import a saved animations/ graph snapshot into model source. Requires expectedRevision and optional graphAsset.

tools.name: animation_editor
tools.description: Open an authoring asset in the animation editor; tab=clips|graph.

tools.name: modeling_preview

tools.name: animation_preview

tools.name: animation_graph_list
tools.description: List animation/rig assets in animations/.

tools.name: animation_graph_get
tools.description: Read an animation/rig asset without executing custom callbacks.

tools.name: animation_graph_validate
tools.description: Compile graph and rig against the selected model. Custom host callbacks require their host registry.

tools.name: animation_graph_set
tools.description: Save an authoring draft; validates topology, not model-specific execution. expected prevents overwriting concurrent edits.

tools.name: animation_graph_apply
tools.description: Validate saved asset against target type model and apply a graph snapshot through rules_set.

tools.description: Validate explicit humanoid bone roles against a model.

tools.name: animation_montage_validate

tools.description: Read versioned avatar/montage/root track/ragdoll animation asset.

tools.name: animation_asset_save
tools.description: Save validated asset with optimistic concurrency. No overwrite without expected.

tools.name: shader_graph_catalog
tools.description: Supported operations and domains; all ports are RGBA vectors, scalar constants splat.

tools.name: shader_graph_list
tools.description: List project shader graph assets.

tools.name: shader_graph_get
tools.description: Read and validate a project graph.

tools.name: shader_graph_validate
tools.description: Validate graph and generate GLSL/MSL statements without writing files.

tools.name: shader_graph_set
tools.description: Validate and atomically save shaders/<name>.json. Existing assets require expected original graph; missing expected means create-only. Applying is separate.

tools.name: shader_graph_apply
tools.description: Apply a saved graph snapshot: target=material library name or existing particle effect name, emitter=0 by default; postfx scope=game|map. Reapply after edits.

tools.name: actor_get
tools.description: Read the actor-session rules (rules.actor) and the open world-space map.

tools.name: actor_set
tools.description: Validate and apply actor-session rules / world-space map atomically. Saves remain explicit.

tools.name: world_simulation_lod_get
tools.description: Inspect normalized shared simulation LOD settings; does not claim live adoption.

tools.name: world_simulation_lod_validate
tools.description: Validate a simulation LOD configuration using the shared native parser; no mutation.

tools.name: world_simulation_lod_set
tools.description: Validate and save authored simulation LOD policy. Requires a restarted compatible simulation; changing content can invalidate existing world saves.

tools.name: world_save_list
tools.description: List private persistent world UUIDs under the saved project. No recovery claim.

tools.name: world_save_create
tools.description: Create a new private world from the saved project. Never overwrite existing saves.

tools.name: world_save_status
tools.description: Recover offline under exclusive lock, report finalized tick, ledger and region counts.

tools.name: world_save_page
tools.description: Read bounded stable ID bootstrap or revision delta; resetRequired means replace projection.

tools.name: world_save_checkpoint

tools.name: world_save_backups
tools.description: List backup metadata or explicitly verify full checkpoint/WAL recovery.

tools.name: world_save_retention_preview

tools.name: world_save_retention_apply

tools.name: world_save_fork
tools.description: Restore a verified generation into an independent empty project world UUID. Source unchanged.

tools.name: world_job_status

tools.name: world_job_cancel

tools.name: world_job_release

tools.name: map_generate
tools.description: Generate the open map with the deterministic map generator (same code as match-time generation): preset (gen_presets), seed, players (1..8), symmetry (auto | none | point | mirror | mirror-y | mirror4 | rot4 | rotational), params (overrides, see gen_presets). The open map's player 1 objects are the start kit and its neutral objects decide what is placed (useTemplate: false = rules heuristics). Result: starts, path lengths between starts (engine pathfinder), connectivity, warnings. Planet presets (rocky, ocean, moon) build a whole planet map: bodies from the open map's world block (or sun + planet + moon), params.layout 'shared' (all players on one body, polar rotational symmetry) or 'separate' (one identical planet each), moons get params.moonResources x the resources. mode: 'bake' (default) writes a static map (undoable); 'match' only stores a 'generate' block so every match generates a new map from the match seed ('seed': 'match'); 'fixed' stores the block with this seed.

tools.name: map_resize
tools.description: Resize the map (keeps the top-left part).

tools.name: map_heightfield
tools.description: Add a flat heightfield (corner heights, all 0) to the open map, or remove it ('enabled': false). Sculpting is done with the terrain tools; the simulation uses the heights when rules terrain.model is 'heightfield'.

tools.name: map_mirror
tools.description: Make the map symmetric: copy the left half to the right ('horizontal') or rotate it 180° ('point'); owners 1 and 2 swap.

tools.name: terrain_paint
tools.description: Paint terrain kind on a rect or circle: ground, water, blocked, nobuild, shallow, ramp, rock. Planets: pass body + face + x, y (or dir) + radius (cells) to paint the cells of a cube-sphere body.

tools.name: terrain_level
tools.description: Set cliff level (0..9) on a rect or circle. Units change level only over 'ramp' cells; higher ground gives the bonuses defined in rules.heights.

tools.name: terrain_height
tools.description: Raise (delta > 0) or lower the visual height smoothly in a circle (cosmetic; gameplay uses levels).

tools.name: field_paint
tools.description: Paint initial values of a grid field on the open map (saved in the map's "gridFields".<id>.values as RLE; undoable). x, z (map cells) + radius (map cells, 0 = one field cell) or rect [x, z, w, h] (map cells); value in field units (fixed fields: decimals); mode set | add | max | erase (back to the default). player = layer of per-player fields.

tools.name: region_paint
tools.description: Paint a region (Northgard-style territory) with a letter (A-Z, '.' erases); optional display name.

tools.name: entity_place
tools.description: Place objects of a type on the map. owner: 0 neutral, 1..N player, -1 hostile creeps. count > 1 places a cluster around x,z ('spread' radius).

tools.name: entity_list
tools.description: List objects on the open map (optionally filtered by type / owner / rect).

tools.name: entity_update
tools.description: Change an object (by id or index): type, owner, x, z, id, garrison, amount; any other key is stored on the object (e.g. inventory {"wood": 20}, null removes).

tools.name: entity_delete
tools.description: Delete an object by id/index, or all objects matching type/owner/rect when 'all' is true.

tools.name: road_toggle
tools.description: Add or remove a road between two objects (ids or indices) — Mushroom Wars style movement graph.

tools.name: player_set
tools.description: Change player N (1-based): name, team, faction, start [x,z] (faction start units spawn there), waves (scripted side), resources {id: amount}, ai {preset: easy|normal|hard|rush|defender|economist, thinkTicks, aggression, any rules ai knob} for this slot's computer player ({} clears it).

tools.name: player_remove
tools.description: Remove player N (their objects become neutral).

tools.name: map_validate
tools.description: Check the open map against the rules and the real game loader. Returns errors and warnings.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last map edit.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone map edit.

tools.name: match_run
tools.description: Run a fast bot-vs-bot match on the open map (headless, deterministic) and report the outcome: winner, duration, per-player economy/army timeline, event counts and fired triggers; optional event log. Use it to balance and to verify a map is playable.

events.description: true = log every event (with time, players, objects), or a list of event names

saveCheck.description: at this second: save, load into a fresh simulation and run both 10 s without bots; reports whether they stay identical

reportMissingNativeModules.description: When the host lacks project modules, return status missing_native_modules and their IDs without running the simulation. Otherwise run the normal check.

tools.name: asset_import
tools.description: Copy a file (model .glb/.gltf, texture .png/.jpg, sound .wav/.ogg, font, UI .rml/.rcss) into the game folder.

source.description: absolute path of the file to import

dest.description: path inside the game folder, e.g. models/tank.glb

tools.name: asset_list
tools.description: List files of the game folder (optionally a subfolder), with sizes.

tools.name: build_start
tools.description: Package the open game for a platform in the background: macos, ios, android, web, windows, linux, all. Poll build_status. A missing toolchain ends the build with exit code 3 and a log line AIVERSE_MISSING_TOOLCHAIN <target>: <ids> (toolchain_check / toolchain_install).

installMissing.description: install missing toolchains first, see toolchain_check

tools.name: build_status
tools.description: State and log tail of the current/last build.

tools.name: view_screenshot
tools.description: Scene screenshot defaults to clean render-texture capture; clean:false keeps viewport UI. Optional width/height render256..4096 up to8MP, pitch -89..89; camera inspection never changes the map.

tools.name: view_focus
tools.description: Move the editor camera to look at x,y,z (y and distance optional).

tools.name: play_start
tools.description: Play-test the open map inside the editor window (bots on all sides unless 'human' is set). The user watches live.

human.description: player slot controlled by the user, 0 = bots only

tools.name: play_stop
tools.description: Stop the play-test and return to editing.

tools.name: region_ownership_diagnostics
tools.description: Read last successful live region ownership reconciliation; requires running editor simulation.

tools.name: play_status
tools.description: Current play-test state: time, players, resources, units, result.

tools.name: play_units
tools.description: Live objects of the running play-test: id (for play_command), map name, type, owner, position, hp, orders, statuses. Filter by owner / type; at most 'limit' (default 200).

tools.name: play_command
tools.description: Issue a player command in the running play-test, exactly like player input (the user sees it live). command: move, attack, stop, hold, patrol, gather, build, train, cancel_train, rally, smart, send, research, place, sell, deploy, ability, reinforce, claim, auto_build, upgrade, surrender, dig, paint_room, pick_up, drop, slap, possess, direct, player_ability, build_road, connect_road, stance, retreat, load, unload, transit, guard, follow, formation, build_line, merge, split, trade, trade_route, tribute, diplomacy, buy_item, use_item, drop_item, pick_item, bounty, rotate, lock, end_turn, script, topdown, topdown_ability, progression, repair, reclaim, self_destruct. units: object references (packed id numbers from play_units, names from map/scenario 'id', or a filter {type, owner, tags, kind, area [x,z,w,h], near [x,z] + radius}); target: one reference; point: 'at' [x, z] or x, z. param by name: 'type' (build/train/upgrade/place), 'tech' (research), 'ability' (ability id of the first unit's type), 'player_ability' (id), 'room' (paint_room), 'percent' (send), 'stance' (aggressive/defensive/hold/passive); or a raw 'param'. load: units board the target transport; unload: units = transports, with a point they drive there first. Rect commands (dig, paint_room, build_road): 'rect' [w, h] at the point with 'extra' (dig: 1 unmark; build_road: 1 remove). 'queue': true appends to the current orders (Shift). script: a rules "commands" command: 'id' + 'args' {name: value} (int / enum name / bool / point [x, z] / unit reference), units = the selection. topdown (rules topDown heroes): 'move' [x, z] stick vector (length = magnitude, at most 1), 'aim' [x, z] aim direction, 'fire' true; sticky until the next topdown command. topdown_ability: 'ability' id of the hero's type, optional point (default: along the aim / facing) or target; 'phase' tap (default) / press / release / cancel, 'dir' [x, z] the button's stick, 'distance' 0..1 of the range; 'escape': true sends the escape destination ('at', or 'dir' + 'distance' of the budget). progression (rules progression level-up offers): 'op' choose / reroll / close / open, 'card' (1-based) of the open offer.

units.description: references: id numbers, names or a filter object

dir.description: conveyors: e / s / w / n; topdown_ability: [x, z] stick direction

card.description: progression: 1-based card of the open offer

tools.name: device_list
tools.description: Device presets for the simulator (phones, tablets, desktops).

tools.name: device_set
tools.description: Show the viewport in a device frame (resolution, notch/safe area, orientation) like a phone simulator. 'none' turns it off.

tools.name: port_scan
tools.description: Inspect a Unity/Godot/Unreal project without writing. path is required; returns engine/version/assets/scenes and errors.

tools.name: port_import
tools.description: Import project path into out, optional scale (metres to cells), mapping (synonym JSON). Returns port report. Preserves edited files. Does not open the result automatically.

tools.name: port_report
tools.description: Read port-report.json in project path. Resolve missing mechanics using rules_schema first, then Lua, then native modules. Verify with scenario_run/bot matches and source screenshots.

tools.name: port_item
tools.description: Read report item id plus serialized components, script source, fields and uses from port.json in project path.

tools.name: port_resolve
tools.description: Mark report item id resolved with how (rules/lua/native/dropped) and reason. Changes report only; verify implementation before resolving.

tools.name: package_search
tools.description: Search the package catalog (AIVERSE-PACKAGES): words match id, titles, summaries, tags and provides. Optional category (materials, textures, models, templates, audio, vfx, ui, scripts, plugins, tools) and kind (content, template, source, script, plugin, tool). Returns [{id, kind, category, title, latest, size, cached}].

tools.name: package_info
tools.description: Full catalog entry of a package: manifest (title, summary, description and their -<lang> translations, licence, minEngine, provides, dependencies, install.mount), versions with sizes and SHA-256, previews, readme, viewer URL.

tools.name: package_add
tools.description: Install a content package into the open project (or project): copies it to install.mount, installs its content dependencies first, merges its material library, records it in game.json packages and aiverse.lock. id may carry a range (terrain-pbr@^1.0). force overwrites differing files and ids.

tools.name: package_remove
tools.description: Remove an installed package from the open project: deletes its files and merged ids, drops it from game.json and aiverse.lock. Dependencies stay installed.

tools.name: package_status
tools.description: Packages of the open project: wanted range (game.json), locked version (aiverse.lock), installed files, missing and changed files. mismatch > 0 means install or verify is needed.

tools.name: package_install
tools.description: Restore every package of the open project from aiverse.lock (after cloning the project).

tools.name: package_skill
tools.description: Packages an engine skill needs (frontmatter packages:). With install=true installs them into the open project.

tools.name: tileset_list
tools.description: Tilesets of the open game (templates/<id>/tilesets/*.json) with their terrains: id, map char, gameplay cell kind, level, resource field, autotile type. The map's tile layer uses one of them.

tools.name: tiles_init
tools.description: Give the open map a tile layer (2D tile games): every cell gets terrain 'fill' (default: the tileset's first), or with fromTerrain=true the first terrain matching each cell's current kind/level. Replaces an existing tile layer.

tools.name: tile_paint
tools.description: Paint a tileset terrain on the map's tile layer at a circle (x, y, radius) or rect [x0,y0,x1,y1]. Edges/corners are chosen automatically (autotile) from neighbours; the terrain's gameplay (cell kind, cliff level, resource field) is written into the map. 'tile' places one exact atlas tile instead (autotile off). Undoable.

tools.name: tile_info
tools.description: What the tile layer has at cell (x, y): terrain and the atlas tiles autotiling picked (under/top).

tools.name: tiles_remove
tools.description: Remove the tile layer of the open map (gameplay terrain stays as baked).

tools.name: terrain_detail
tools.description: The map's visual detail heightmap (terrain.detail: k samples per cell, sub-cell relief; docs/terrain.md). action: 'info' (scale, size, min/max, deviation from the simulation surface), 'create' (scale 1/2/4/8, from the surface drawn now: smooth style = organic cliffs / bicubic relief), 'remove'. Sculpting with terrain_sculpt {detail:true} creates it on demand. Visual only; on heightfield maps the corners follow it. Undoable. Planets: pass body (id) for that body's detail grid (6 faces x (N*scale+1)^2 samples; seams equal; maps/<map>.<body>.detail.r16 on save).

body.description: planet / moon id of the map world block

tools.name: terrain_paint_material
tools.description: Paint a terrain material layer (index 0..3 of the visual terrain.layers) at detail resolution: soft brush at x, y (world units, fractions allowed), radius in world units, strength 0..1, hardness 0..1; 'points' for a stroke. Creates the detail layer (scale 4) when missing. Visual only. Undoable.

tools.name: terraweave_excavate
tools.description: Dig or fill a radius in the current flat grid heightfield. Center xCm/zCm, radiusCm and depthCm use world centimetres. Never creates caves/undercuts; preserves authored detail material and fine surface by rebasing the detail onto changed corners. Undoable.

tools.name: terraweave_sparse_paint
tools.description: Paint or create TerraWeave terrain at any signed world-centimetre coordinate. Missing chunks touched by the brush appear automatically; neighbors use the same global Earthworks heights. Flat chunk renders as one quad at every camera distance. State saved in map.terraweaveSparse; undoable.

tools.name: terraweave_caverns_pick
tools.description: Read-only SDF surface raycast in cm and normalized Q20 direction.

tools.name: terraweave_caverns_paint
tools.description: Author carve/fill spherical cave SDF stamps in signed world centimetres. Use erase with stampId or get to inspect; settings changes the generator recipe, entrance_add/update/erase author shafts. MapDoc persistence, undo/redo, MCP and HTML5 share this operation. Caller owns runtime chunk invalidation.

tools.name: terraweave_preview
tools.description: Preview 9x9 deterministic TerraWeave heights in cm, no map mutations. Use terraweave_generate to bake the full heightfield; flat grid map only.

tools.name: terraweave_generate
tools.description: Generate full deterministic TerraWeave heightfield in the current grid map. By default refuses to overwrite existing sculpt/detail. Set overwrite=true to explicitly replace authored terrain, or preserveEdits=true to move the existing authored height and detail residuals onto a new generator base (requires a matching saved TerraWeave recipe fingerprint). Both choices are mutually exclusive. Creates one undo step.

tools.name: terraweave_meadow_get
tools.description: Read the authored grass meadow; null uses the legacy generator.

tools.name: terraweave_meadow_set
tools.description: Set the map meadow preset or custom species configuration. Undoable.

tools.name: terraweave_forest_get
tools.description: Read the map's TerraWeave forest recipe (extra.terraweaveForest, defaults when absent) and the saved terrain recipe (extra.terraweave). Read-only.

tools.name: terraweave_forest_set
tools.description: Save the TerraWeave forest recipe into the map (extra.terraweaveForest): enabled, spacingCm 300..5000, densityPermille 0..1000, maxSlopePermille 0..5000, seedOffset >= 0. Drives the deterministic TerraWeave Arbor forest overlay (no entity per tree). One undo step.

tools.name: erosion_zones
tools.description: List the map's erosion zones (map key erosionZones): id, shape circle{x,z,radius} | polygon{points [[x,z],...]}, soil sand|silt|loam|clay|gravel|rock, coefficient 0..10 (x the default bank erosion rate; 0 = protected).

tools.name: erosion_zone_set
tools.description: Create or replace (by id) an erosion zone: where the ground erodes and how fast. shape circle (x, z, radius m) or polygon (points [[x,z],...] m, 3..256); soil sand|silt|loam|clay|gravel|rock (optional); coefficient 0..10 (1 = default rate, 0 = does not erode). Used by the NEREID -> TerraWeave bank erosion (applyErosionZones). Undoable.

tools.name: erosion_zone_delete
tools.description: Delete an erosion zone by id. Undoable.

tools.name: terrain_sculpt
tools.description: Sculpt the terrain. op: raise | lower (strength = world units at the centre), smooth | flatten | erode (strength 0..1), noise (strength = amplitude), set (strength = target height), stamp (strength = height of the brush image; 'stamp': crater | mesa | dunes | rocks or a grayscale PNG in the game folder, 'angle' degrees). x, y: centre in world units (fractions allowed), radius in world units; 'points' [[x,y],...] applies the dab along a stroke. detail=true (default when the map has a detail layer) sculpts the visual detail heightmap at sub-cell resolution (k samples per cell, soft falloff, 'hardness' 0..1; created from the drawn surface on first use; erode / stamp need it); detail=false sculpts the cell corners (heightfield; the first sculpt creates it from the current surface). Corners are gameplay only with rules terrain.model 'heightfield' (they then follow the detail). Undoable. Planets: pass body + face + x, y (cells on that face) or dir [x,y,z]; radius in cells; the brush is 3D and crosses face seams. detail=true (default when the body has a detail grid) sculpts the body's detail grid (sub-cell radius, hardness; created on first use, corners follow).

body.description: planet / moon id of the map world block

dir.description: surface direction [x, y, z] instead of face/x/y

tools.name: terrain_heights
tools.description: Read the visual surface height (world units) at points [[x,y],...] (or a w x h grid summary when 'grid': step in cells): min, max, mean. Uses the same surface as the renderer (detail heightmap, else heightfield corners, else levels + ramps + fine heights).

tools.name: terrain_material
tools.description: Paint the terrain material layer (index 0..3 into the game's visual terrain.layers, see rules/game.json 'terrain'; -1 erases = by cell kind) on a circle x, y, radius. Visual only (map key terrainMaterial). Undoable. Planets: pass body + face + x, y (or dir) + radius; layer -1 = by cell kind.

body.description: planet / moon id of the map world block

dir.description: surface direction [x, y, z] instead of face/x/y

tools.name: heightmap_export
tools.description: Write the map's heightfield as a 16-bit grayscale PNG ((w+1) x (h+1) pixels; detail=true: the detail heightmap, (w*k+1) x (h*k+1)) to 'file' (relative to the game folder). Returns scale (world units of the 0..65535 range) and offset (height of 0) needed to import it back.

tools.name: heightmap_import
tools.description: Replace the map's heightfield with a grayscale PNG (8 or 16 bit; resampled to (w+1) x (h+1) corners). height = offset + value / 65535 * scale (world units). detail=true (+ 'detailScale' 1..8, default 4): import into the detail heightmap at (w*k+1) x (h*k+1) samples (heightfield maps: corners follow). 'file' is relative to the game folder. Undoable.

tools.name: gen_presets
tools.description: List the map generator presets (built into the engine + the game's rules 'mapgen.presets'): id, title, genre, default params. Planet presets (rocky, ocean, moon) build a whole planet map (map_generate) or one body's terrain (world.bodies[].generate).

tools.name: game_file_read
tools.description: Read a text data file of the open game (path relative to the game folder): lang/ru.json, audio.json, tilesets/desert.json, ui/hud.rml, fx/*.json, ... Use rules_get / map_get for rules.json and maps.

tools.name: game_file_write
tools.description: Create or replace a text data file of the open game (lang/*.json, audio.json, tilesets/*.json, fx/*.json, ui/*.rml|rcss, campaign texts). JSON files are checked before saving. rules.json, game.json and maps have their own ops (rules_set, set_manifest, map_*), which validate against the engine.

tools.name: territory_paint
tools.description: Paint the map's starting territory layer (dungeon / territory-war games): cells owned by player 1..9, 0 clears. Shape: rect [x0,y0,x1,y1] or circle [cx,cy,r]. Only ground cells count in the game.

tools.name: build_estimate
tools.description: Estimated build size for a platform before building: runs aiversebuild --estimate (the real content pack with the game's settings: atlases, sound profile, packaging.files rules, split), returns pack size, atlas stats and the heaviest files. Per-file settings live in game.json packaging.files [{match, exclude, level (0 = store), maxSize, scale}] (packaging.targets.<t>.files for one platform), set with set_manifest.

tools.name: ui_contract
tools.description: How to replace or restyle the game UI: documents the client loads (the game's ui/<name> overrides engine/ui/<name>, also for linked .rcss / images / fonts), the data model "game" (variables, item fields), event callbacks and required element ids. Write files with game_file_write, images with asset_import.

tools.name: balance_batch
tools.description: Many bot-vs-bot matches on the open map over consecutive seeds: win rate per player slot and per faction, match length (avg/median/min/max), timeouts, what gets built and lost per game, types the bots never build. 'factions' {"1": id, ...} overrides the map's factions; 'mirror' swaps the two factions on every other run so map-side advantage and faction strength separate. Nothing is saved.

reportMissingNativeModules.description: When the host lacks project modules, return status missing_native_modules and their IDs without running the simulation. Otherwise run the normal check.

tools.name: balance_duel
tools.description: Arena fight on an empty field: group a vs group b attack-moving into each other, several seeds. Reports win rate, survivors, hp left and cost efficiency (enemy value destroyed per own value lost). 'equalCost' sizes b to a's cost. a / b: {"type": id, "count": n} or a type id.

reportMissingNativeModules.description: When the host lacks project modules, return status missing_native_modules and their IDs without running the simulation. Otherwise run the normal check.

tools.name: balance_matrix
tools.description: Who counters whom: every listed combat unit (default: all with weapons and a cost, up to 10) fights every other with the same resource budget. Returns the win-rate table (row vs column) and a ranking.

reportMissingNativeModules.description: When the host lacks project modules, return status missing_native_modules and their IDs without running the simulation. Otherwise run the normal check.

tools.name: balance_stats
tools.description: Numbers of every unit type side by side: cost, hp, armor, speed, range, DPS per armor type (with the damage table), DPS and effective hp per cost. 'structures': include buildings; 'type': one type.

tools.name: scene_entity_list
tools.description: List document entities with identity and real component data. Light IDs persist; other legacy IDs are provisional.

tools.name: scene_entity_get
tools.description: Read one scene entity and its components by entityId.

tools.name: scene_component_set
tools.description: Patch a declared editable component by entityId and componentId; native validation and Undo history, explicit map_save to persist.

tools.name: scene_light_create
tools.description: Create a Light entity with Transform and Light components in grid or world-space maps. Position is [x,height,z]; on grid maps height is relative to terrain.

tools.name: scene_light_delete
tools.description: Delete a Light entity by persistent ID; rejects other entity kinds. Undoable until explicit map_save.

tools.name: scene_render_lighting_get
tools.description: Read validated map GI and direct lighting settings (renderLighting v1).

tools.name: scene_render_lighting_set
tools.description: Patch map renderLighting v1 settings; native validation, Undo history, explicit map_save. Does not imply hardware support.

tools.name: light_list
tools.description: Decorative lights of the open map ('lights') and its 'lighting' block (time of day, dayLength, clouds, storm).

tools.name: light_add
tools.description: Add a decorative point light to the map (lantern, campfire, lava glow): x, z in cells; height above ground (default 1); color [r,g,b] 0..1; radius in cells (default 4); intensity (default 1.5); flicker 0..1 for fire; halo = glow sprite size. type 'spot' makes a searchlight / lamp cone: angle, pitch, yaw (0 = +x, 90 = +z), sweep for a swinging searchlight. Shown once the cell is explored. Cheap on every quality tier, including old Android.

type.description: spot = searchlight / lamp cone; sphere / tube = area sources shaded as such by Luma direct lighting (a point elsewhere)

nightOnly.description: on at dusk, off at dawn

electric.description: affected by power / damage (map lights: always powered)

bake.description: light baker (lightbake_bake): mixed = realtime + baked bounce, baked = only baked (realtime light off once baked)

tools.name: light_update
tools.description: Change a decorative map light by index (fields as in light_add; omitted fields are kept).

type.description: spot = searchlight / lamp cone; sphere / tube = area sources shaded as such by Luma direct lighting (a point elsewhere)

nightOnly.description: on at dusk, off at dawn

electric.description: affected by power / damage (map lights: always powered)

bake.description: light baker (lightbake_bake): mixed = realtime + baked bounce, baked = only baked (realtime light off once baked)

tools.name: light_delete
tools.description: Delete a decorative map light by index, or all of them with all=true.

tools.name: lighting_set
tools.description: Set the map's 'lighting' block (overrides game.json 'lighting', which set_manifest edits): time 0..1 (0 midnight, 0.25 dawn, 0.5 noon, 0.75 dusk), dayLength = game seconds per day (0 = time stays), nightLevel 0..1, clouds 0..1, cloudStrength, cloudScale, wind [x,z] cells/s, storm 0..1 (overcast + lightning), preset desert | snow | volcanic | overcast | cave (cave = underground: permanent night, only lights). Omitted fields are kept; remove=true deletes the block.

tools.name: view_lighting
tools.description: Editor preview of time of day / clouds / storm (does not change the map): time 0..1, clouds 0..1, storm 0..1; off=true returns to the map's own lighting. Combine with view_screenshot to check night scenes.

tools.name: physis_get
tools.description: Read the open map's authored PHYSIS config and document revision. Includes a default config for new maps. Not live simulation state.

tools.name: physis_validate
tools.description: Validate a complete PHYSIS authoring config without changing the map. config:null validates explicit removal. Does not install or tick a simulation.

tools.name: physis_set
tools.description: Atomically replace the open map's PHYSIS config with Undo/Redo. Read physis_get first and supply its revision as expectedRevision; stale edits fail. config:null removes the block. Does not save files or apply live/remote simulation changes.

tools.name: fx_list
tools.description: Particle effects of the open game (fx/*.json): emitters, looping, lifetime, textures, load errors; where each is bound in fx/fx.json, and the bindings' warnings.

tools.name: fx_get
tools.description: Read an effect (name without .json; 'fx' = the event bindings): raw text and the parsed JSON. Format: engine/fx/FxEffect.h (top comment lists every key incl. trails, sub-emitters, noise, lights), bindings: engine/fx/GameFx.h.

tools.name: fx_set
tools.description: Create or replace an effect (name without .json; 'fx' = the event bindings) from 'json' (object) or 'text'. Validated with the engine's loader first: unknown keys, out-of-range values and missing particle sources are errors with the exact path (emitters[1].trail.time: must be in 0.01..10); missing textures / sub-effects are warnings. Then fx_preview to look at it.

tools.name: fx_delete
tools.description: Delete an effect file. Refuses while fx.json or another effect's subEmitters use it, unless 'unbind': true (removes those bindings; sub-emitter references are only reported).

tools.name: fx_templates
tools.description: Ready effect recipes (built-in textures only, quality tiers set): explosion, fire, smoke, muzzle_flash, magic_aura, heal, frost, lightning, blood, dust_trail, rain, snow, portal, level_up. tools.name: fx_volume_validate
tools.description: Validate a SpectraFX volume asset v1 and resolve its optional project SDF.

tools.name: fx_volume_probe
tools.description: Run 0..8 fixed headless volume ticks and return aggregate field statistics and optional ray integration; CPU reference, no GPU or scene mutation.

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_list
tools.description: List named project Replay Presets in content/spectrafx/replays; bounded metadata only.

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_get

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_check

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_relocate_preview

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_relocate_apply

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_portable_export

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_portable_apply

tools.name: fx_replay_package_list
tools.description: List project-local .aivfx transfer archives; payload validation occurs at preview.

tools.name: fx_replay_package_export
tools.description: Export a verified named preset and recorded dependency bytes to project/packages/<package>.aivfx.

tools.name: fx_replay_package_preview
tools.description: Preview project-local .aivfx package payload installation; reuse maps original content paths to selected target GUIDs.

tools.name: fx_replay_package_apply
tools.description: Install reviewed missing payloads without overwriting; returns portable recipe for separate verified preset import.

tools.name: fx_replay_preset_save

tools.name: fx_graph_validate

tools.name: fx_graph_set

tools.name: fx_graph_delete
tools.description: Delete a SpectraFX graph asset by name. Does not affect separately baked fx/*.json effects.

tools.name: fx_graph_node_catalog
tools.description: List SpectraFX v1/v2 authoring node types, categories, starter properties and typed data input ports.

tools.name: fx_graph_edit
tools.description: Apply a v1/v2 graph edit in memory and return the edited JSON plus compiler diagnostics. tools.name: fx_graph_draft_set
tools.description: Save an incomplete SpectraFX graph in fx/graphs/_drafts/<name>.vfx.json without changing published assets. Return compiler diagnostics but do not reject disconnected drafts.

tools.name: fx_graph_draft_get
tools.description: Read a saved incomplete SpectraFX v1/v2 draft, including validation diagnostics.

tools.name: fx_graph_draft_list
tools.description: List SpectraFX draft graph names without publishing them.

tools.name: fx_graph_draft_publish
tools.description: Validate a draft and publish to fx/graphs/<name>.vfx.json; invalid drafts remain private and never replace the working asset.

tools.name: fx_graph_bake
tools.description: Compile a SpectraFX graph into legacy fx/<effect>.json so fx_preview and existing game/event bindings can use it. Refuses to replace an effect unless overwrite=true.

tools.name: fx_graph_preview

tools.name: overlay_preview
tools.description: Editor preview: draw these overlays in the Scene and Game views regardless of their 'when' (selected-entity overlays use every object when nothing is selected, event overlays spawn sample popups). placeType = a structure type id to preview ghost / placement overlays at the cursor or the view centre. off=true ends the preview. tools.name: branding_get
tools.description: Game icons and splash screen: game.json 'icons' (master image >= 1024 px + per-platform overrides: ios, macos, android {legacy, round, foreground, background, monochrome}, windows, web, linux; padding/background/cornerRadius for opaque icons) and 'splash' (background, image/frames/sheet, fit, logos with animation keyframes or fadeIn/fadeOut/pulse/rotate/slide/zoom, minSeconds, maxSeconds, loop, skippable, progress bar, native launch screen). tools.name: branding_set
tools.description: Set game.json 'icons' and/or 'splash' (validated before saving; images are project-relative paths). Pass null to remove a block; merge=true merges objects into the existing blocks (null values remove keys). Check the result with icons_preview / splash_preview.

tools.name: icons_preview
tools.description: Render every icon the build generates (iOS, macOS, Android legacy/round/adaptive with circle and squircle masks, Windows .ico sizes, web favicon/apple-touch/PWA/maskable, Linux hicolor) at real pixel size into one PNG contact sheet you can look at.

tools.name: splash_preview
tools.description: Render the splash screen at a few moments of its timeline (default: 5 frames over the logo sequence) into a PNG strip, with the progress bar as if loading took the minimum time. width/height of each frame in pixels (default 320x180, portrait games 180x320).

tools.name: planet_forest_get
tools.description: Read the authored planetary forest, catalogue, marker/body IDs and current revision. Not live ECS.

tools.name: planet_forest_set
tools.description: Replace complete forest ecology/weather/plant config and ARBOR catalogue atomically; null inherits/removes. Read current mapPath/revision with planet_forest_get first.

tools.name: planet_forest_plant
tools.description: Create one authored plant at face-local coordinates or existing surface marker, allocating a stable key. Not a live spawn.

tools.name: planet_forest_move

tools.name: planet_forest_remove
tools.description: Remove exactly one authored plant by species/key; never delete its shared marker entity or modify live ECS.

tools.name: planet_info
tools.description: Bodies of the open map's world block (planets, moons, stars): id, kind, radius, faceSize, seaLevel, orbit, corner height range. Planet tools take body + face (0..5) + x, y in cells (docs/planets.md).

tools.name: scenario_run
tools.description: Headless scripted test of a mechanic on a copy of the open map (nothing is saved): place named objects, give commands at given seconds, let bots play some slots, then get event and trigger logs, watched objects and pass/fail checks. Commands: move, attack, stop, hold, patrol, gather, build, train, cancel_train, rally, smart, send, research, place, sell, deploy, ability, reinforce, claim, auto_build, upgrade, surrender, dig, paint_room, pick_up, drop, slap, possess, direct, player_ability, build_road, connect_road, stance, retreat, load, unload, transit, guard, follow, formation, build_line, merge, split, trade, trade_route, tribute, diplomacy, buy_item, use_item, drop_item, pick_item, bounty, rotate, lock, end_turn, script, topdown, topdown_ability, progression, repair, reclaim, self_destruct. units: object references (packed id numbers from play_units, names from map/scenario 'id', or a filter {type, owner, tags, kind, area [x,z,w,h], near [x,z] + radius}); target: one reference; point: 'at' [x, z] or x, z. param by name: 'type' (build/train/upgrade/place), 'tech' (research), 'ability' (ability id of the first unit's type), 'player_ability' (id), 'room' (paint_room), 'percent' (send), 'stance' (aggressive/defensive/hold/passive); or a raw 'param'. load: units board the target transport; unload: units = transports, with a point they drive there first. Rect commands (dig, paint_room, build_road): 'rect' [w, h] at the point with 'extra' (dig: 1 unmark; build_road: 1 remove). 'queue': true appends to the current orders (Shift). script: a rules "commands" command: 'id' + 'args' {name: value} (int / enum name / bool / point [x, z] / unit reference), units = the selection. topdown (rules topDown heroes): 'move' [x, z] stick vector (length = magnitude, at most 1), 'aim' [x, z] aim direction, 'fire' true; sticky until the next topdown command. topdown_ability: 'ability' id of the hero's type, optional point (default: along the aim / facing) or target; 'phase' tap (default) / press / release / cancel, 'dir' [x, z] the button's stick, 'distance' 0..1 of the range; 'escape': true sends the escape destination ('at', or 'dir' + 'distance' of the budget). progression (rules progression level-up offers): 'op' choose / reroll / close / open, 'card' (1-based) of the open offer. Event names: spawned, died, attack, hit, trainStarted, trained, buildPlaced, built, gathered, captured, playerDefeated, notEnough, researched, levelUp, ability, miss, readyToPlace, sold, regionClaimed, wave, lowPower, upgraded, message, dug, territory, roomPainted, recruited, creatureLeft, pickedUp, dropped, slapped, possessed, payday, playerAbility, produced, delivered, roadBuilt, lanesChanged, statusStart, statusEnd, areaStart, areaTrigger, areaEnd, projectileLaunch, impact, chainJump, castStart, channelStart, channelEnd, alert, garrisonChanged, transitStart, transitEnd, triggerFired, loaded, unloaded, cyclePhase, traded, diplomacy, item, merged, objective, dialog, camera, missionEnd, learned, crewKilled, crewed, infected, submerged, trapFired, groupTeleport, paved, morale, turn, fortified.

clear.description: start from an empty copy of the map: no objects, roads, waves or start units; victory never triggers

spawn.description: [{id, type, owner (1..N, 0 neutral, -1 creeps), at [x, z], count, spacing, garrison, amount}] - a count > 1 names members id#1..id#N and 'id' refers to all of them

commands.description: [{t: seconds, command, player (default 1), ...}] - same keys as play_command

checks.description: [{t?: seconds (default: at the end), name?, one of alive|dead|count|hp|resource+player|event|trigger|variable|distance+to|status+on|result, comparison '>=' '>' '<=' '<' '==' '!=': number}]

watch.description: references to report at the end (and every 'every' seconds in a timeline)

events.description: true = log every event, or a list of event names

bots.description: player slots played by the AI, or "all"

reportMissingNativeModules.description: When the host lacks project modules, return status missing_native_modules and their IDs without running the simulation. Otherwise run the normal check.

tools.name: campaign_get
tools.description: Read the game's campaign.json (missions: id, name, map, briefing, next, carry). Empty when the game has none.

tools.name: campaign_set
tools.description: Write campaign.json: {"start": id, "missions": [{"id", "name", "map", "briefing", "next", "carry": {"resources": [...], "tags": [...], "types": [...], "max": n}}]}. Missions end with the trigger action endMission (result, next) or a normal victory; objectives, dialog and camera are trigger actions too.

tools.name: campaign_run
tools.description: Play the campaign headless from a mission (default: start): bots on every side, each mission until it ends or 'seconds'; survivors and resources are carried as the mission's 'carry' says. Reports each mission's outcome, objectives and the carry.

tools.name: rules_lint
tools.description: Find keys in rules.json and the open map that the game loader never reads (typos like 'helth', blocks in the wrong place), with the closest key the loader expects there. Runs the real loader; presentation blocks (view, sprite, lights) are skipped.

tools.name: rules_schema

'path' narrows keys to a prefix, e.g. 'types.*.weapons'. Read this before editing rules.

tools.name: rules_prune
tools.description: Find keys in rules.json (and its included files) set to exactly the value the engine uses when the key is missing, so they can be dropped: a smaller rules file, the same game. Runs the real loader; skips presentation blocks, level overrides and entries in "extends" chains. apply: true removes them, checks a bot match on the open map gives the same checksums, and saves (each part back to its file).

tools.name: material_techniques_get
tools.description: List a model's material names and ordered technique rules.

tools.name: material_techniques_set
tools.description: Replace technique rules. Use [] to clear. Pass the previous rules as expected to detect a concurrent edit.

tools.name: material_list
tools.description: The game's material library (materials.json) and, per type with a model, its material overrides, node assignments, the model's own material names and mesh nodes (targets for material_apply).

tools.name: material_triplanar
tools.description: Build a UV-free world-space material. Color and optional OpenGL tangent normal maps repeat every repeatMetres world units. Save the returned material with material_set and assign with material_apply.

tools.name: material_get
tools.description: One library material, flattened with its "base" chain.

tools.description: Create or replace a material in the game's library (materials.json), usable by name from any type: material_apply, or a view's "materials" / "assign". Material keys: color [r,g,b(,a)] linear 0..1, metallic 0..1, roughness 0..1, thinTransmission 0..1, shadowDiffusion 0..1 world units, sssStrength 0..1, sssScale 0..1, sssThickness 0..1 world units (0 = artistic backlight), sssColor [r,g,b] linear 0..1, emissive [r,g,b], emissiveStrength, alpha opaque|mask|blend|additive|additive-unweighted, cutoff, doubleSided, unlit, castShadow, receiveShadow, vertexColors, team tint|mask|alpha|vertex|none, teamStrength, texture / normalMap / emissiveMap / teamMask (PNG/JPEG/TGA/KTX2 paths in the game folder, e.g. made by texture_generate), metallicRoughnessMap (glTF layout: G roughness, B metallic) / occlusionMap (R) with occlusionStrength, normalScale, uvScale [u,v] tiling, uvOffset [u,v], base (inherit another library material), replace (start from a blank material instead of the model's), description. merge: true keeps the existing keys and changes only the given ones.

tools.description: Give a type's model a material: a library name ("steel") or an inline material object. target = a material name of the model (material_list shows them) or "*" for all: the material's keys override that material (textures are kept unless given; replace: true starts blank). node = a mesh node name or glob ("Turret", "Wheel*"): the meshes of that node and of everything under it get a fresh material. remove: true deletes the override / assignment. Material keys: color [r,g,b(,a)] linear 0..1, metallic 0..1, roughness 0..1, thinTransmission 0..1, shadowDiffusion 0..1 world units, sssStrength 0..1, sssScale 0..1, sssThickness 0..1 world units (0 = artistic backlight), sssColor [r,g,b] linear 0..1, emissive [r,g,b], emissiveStrength, alpha opaque|mask|blend|additive|additive-unweighted, cutoff, doubleSided, unlit, castShadow, receiveShadow, vertexColors, team tint|mask|alpha|vertex|none, teamStrength, texture / normalMap / emissiveMap / teamMask (PNG/JPEG/TGA/KTX2 paths in the game folder, e.g. made by texture_generate), metallicRoughnessMap (glTF layout: G roughness, B metallic) / occlusionMap (R) with occlusionStrength, normalScale, uvScale [u,v] tiling, uvOffset [u,v], base (inherit another library material), replace (start from a blank material instead of the model's), description.

tools.description: Inspect a project PNG/JPEG/HDR/uncompressed EXR/DDS/KTX2 and return its immutable source revision, dimensions and format.

tools.name: texture_graph_dependency_revisions
tools.description: Read current SHA-256 revisions of bounded project image dependencies, without decoding or writing.

tools.description: Native typed procedural CPU node catalog.

tools.description: Validated native PBR starter graph documents.

tools.description: List saved texture graph documents.

tools.name: texture_graph_get
tools.description: Read saved source graph.

tools.name: texture_graph_validate
tools.description: Validate types, topology, parameters and work budget without evaluating or writing.

tools.name: texture_graph_set
tools.description: Save validated graph; existing source requires matching expected document. No texture bake.

tools.name: texture_graph_preview
tools.description: Evaluate one node or output at up to 32x32, return actual RGBA8 hex without disk writes.
