tools.name: postfx_enable
tools.description: Switch the whole post-processing chain on or off (game.json, or per map) without deleting the effects.

scope.description: game = game.json (all maps, default); map = the open map only (overrides game.json per effect type)

tools.name: postfx_estimate
tools.description: Frame cost of a post-processing chain without changing anything: pass "effects" (array as in game.json) to try a combination, or nothing for the current game + map chain. Per device class: tier, ms, passes, fps at 60, warnings.

tools.name: postfx_lut_neutral
tools.description: Write a neutral colour lookup table (PNG strip, Unreal layout) into the game folder: grade it in any image editor together with a screenshot, then postfx_add {type: 'lut', texture: <path>}. size 16 (256x16) or 32 (1024x32, default).

tools.name: view_postfx
tools.description: Editor preview of post-processing (does not change the game): quality off | low | medium | high shows what weak phones (low) or strong devices (high) get; scene=false hides effects in the Scene view (Game view keeps them). Combine with view_screenshot to compare tiers.

tools.name: script_list
tools.description: Lua scripts of the open game: every scripts/**/*.lua with whether rules/map list it as a simulation script ("scripts") or a view script ("viewScripts"). Reference: script_api.

tools.name: script_read
tools.description: Read a Lua script of the open game (path scripts/....lua).

tools.name: script_write
tools.description: Create or replace a Lua script (scripts/....lua). It is compiled first and NOT saved when it has a syntax error (the error is returned with file:line). Simulation scripts must not use float literals (use fx("1.5"), fx(3, 2) or integers). register=true adds it to rules.json "scripts" (or "viewScripts" for scripts/view/...). A running play-test restarts with the new scripts.

tools.name: script_check
tools.description: Compile every script of the open game and run a headless bot match on the open map for `seconds` (default 60): returns syntax errors, runtime errors (file:line) and the script log. Run it after script_write.

reportMissingNativeModules.description: When the host lacks project modules, return status missing_native_modules and their IDs without running the simulation. Otherwise run the normal check.

tools.name: script_api
tools.description: Reference of the Lua scripting API (events, game.* queries and actions, fx numbers, data hooks, view scripts) as JSON. Read it before writing scripts; the full guide is docs/scripting.md.

tools.name: toolchain_check
tools.description: What building for a target needs on this machine (cmake, Emscripten, JDK 17, Android SDK/NDK, Gradle, Xcode, Visual Studio, ...): per requirement id, name, found, path, version, why it is missing, whether it installs automatically, what the installer does and the download size. 'missing' lists required ids; 'hostSupported' false = this OS can't build the target at all.

tools.name: toolchain_install
tools.description: Install what a target needs (or one requirement id from toolchain_check: emsdk, cmake, jdk, android-sdk, android-ndk, android-cmake, gradle, xcode-clt) into ~/.aiverse/toolchains, in the background with progress in the build log. Poll build_status, then call toolchain_check again. Downloads can be large (Emscripten ~400 MB, Android NDK ~700 MB).

tools.name: native_status
tools.description: C++ modules of the open project (rules.json nativeModules) against what this editor binary has compiled in: required, compiled, missing; the per-project editor build (<project>/Builds/.temp/editor-<host>): buildDir, editor / headless binary paths, built, buildModules, upToDate (newer than native/ sources and the engine binary), ready (up to date and has every module: the editor switches to it on open without asking), why. See docs/native-modules.md.

tools.name: native_build
tools.description: Configure + build the engine for the open project (-DAIVERSE_CONTENT_DIR=<project>, Release, targets aiverse_editor + aiverse_headless + aiverse_client: the AiverseGame the editor launches then has the project's modules too) into <project>/Builds/.temp/editor-<host> (git-ignored; never touches the engine checkout). Output streams into the build log: poll build_status, then native_status. wait=true blocks until the build ends (aiversemcp without the editor; inside the editor the window freezes meanwhile). Returns the editor / headless / client binary paths. Restart into it: GUI only.

tools.name: strategic_load
tools.description: Load a strategic (campaign) map for the open game: provinces {id, adj, owner, income, pos, terrain}, armies {owner, at, units: {type: count}}, players, start resources, recruit costs, movesPerTurn, battle {mode: auto|simulate, seconds, size}. 'file' (project-relative, e.g. strategic.json) or 'def' inline. Battles use the game's rules.json.

tools.name: strategic_state
tools.description: The whole strategic state: provinces with owners, armies with units and strength, treasury, battle log.

tools.name: strategic_order
tools.description: Give an order for the current player (or 'player'): {"move": {"army": id, "to": province}} (an enemy army there means a battle), {"recruit": {"province", "type", "count"}}, or {"end_turn": true}.

tools.name: strategic_bots
tools.description: Bots play 'turns' player turns (default 10) for 'players' (default: all). 'battle': auto | simulate (play every battle on the RTS simulation with bots; slower). Returns the battles fought and the result.

tools.name: strategic_battle_map
tools.description: The RTS map of the battle the army 'army' would fight by moving to province 'to' (attacker = player 1 on the left). Save it with map_save / play it in the Game window, then report the result with strategic_order as usual (auto) or use battle mode simulate.

tools.name: strategic_save
tools.description: Write the strategic state to the project ('file', default strategic_save.json); strategic_load reads it back.

tools.name: ui_api
tools.description: Reference for building the game's own screens (meta menus: home, levels, shop, profile, settings, rewards, popups): files, the Lua API (ui / profile / shop / game / store / ads), the data model "meta" bound in documents, CSS classes of screens.rcss, events and templates. Read it before ui_screen_create / game_file_write.

tools.name: ui_screen_list
tools.description: The game's own screens: ui/screens/*.rml (name, title, size), ui/screens.json (start, afterMatch, popups), whether ui/profile.json, ui/shop.json, ui/main.lua exist, and the templates ui_screen_create can use.

tools.name: ui_screen_create
tools.description: Create a screen ui/screens/<name>.rml from a template (blank, home, levels, shop, profile, settings, result, dialog — ui_api lists them). Also writes what it needs when the game has none yet: ui/screens.json (the first screen or start:true becomes the start screen, replacing the engine main menu; template result becomes afterMatch; popup:true or template dialog registers a popup), ui/profile.json, ui/shop.json. Then edit the file with game_file_write and check it with ui_preview.

tools.name: ui_screen_delete
tools.description: Delete ui/screens/<name>.rml (and its entries in ui/screens.json).

tools.name: ui_screens_config
tools.description: Edit ui/screens.json: start (first screen; replaces the engine main menu; "" removes it and brings the engine menu back), afterMatch (screen opened after every match with params.result), popup screens.

tools.name: ui_validate
tools.description: Check the game's screens and UI scripts: Lua syntax of ui/**/*.lua and every <script> in ui/**/*.rml, screens named in ui.open / popup / replace / reset / start and screens.json exist, "@key" and game.tr('key') texts exist in every language of the game (engine keys count), JSON data files parse. Returns issues (empty = fine).

tools.name: ui_preview
tools.description: Render a screen of the game in the real game client and return a PNG: the game's start screen, or 'screen' (popups open over the start screen) with 'params' (ui.open parameters) and 'profile' (fields merged into a scratch profile: the player's save is never touched). Size: 'device' (ui_api / device_list ids, e.g. iphone-x, pixel-7) + 'landscape' (the device's safe area is applied and its cut-out drawn), or width / height; 'lang'. 'lua' runs after the screen opens (switch a tab, fill a list). Returns the image and the client log (Lua errors, RmlUi warnings). Needs a display (desktop).

frame.description: draw the device cut-out and home indicator, default true

tools.name: field_list
tools.description: Grid fields of the open game (rules.json "fields" + map "gridFields" overrides, docs/fields.md): per-cell int / fixed layers updated by C++ kernels (decay, diffuse, spread, flow, consume) with per-cell effects (damage, speed, blockMove, blockVision, status, yield, reveal). For each: type, resolution, perPlayer, default/min/max, kernels, effects, size in field cells and the map's initial values (non-default cells, max).

tools.name: field_get
tools.description: Initial values of a grid field on the open map: 'rect' [x, z, w, h] in field cells (at most 64 x 64) gives 'rows' of numbers; without rect an ASCII preview of the whole field ('ascii': '.' default, 1-9 by value, '#' max), at most 96 columns. player = layer of a per-player field. With 'live': true and a running play-test, the current simulation values.

tools.name: field_set_rules
tools.description: Add / replace / delete a grid field definition (docs/fields.md): target 'rules' (default) writes rules.json "fields".<id>, target 'map' writes the open map's "gridFields".<id> parameters (overrides of a rules field, or a map-only field; initial values are kept). 'field' = the definition {type, resolution, default, min, max, perPlayer, kernels, effects, view}; merge=true merges keys into the existing entry; delete=true removes it. Validated against the game's rules before saving.

tools.name: raid_info
tools.description: Extraction raid of the open game (rules.json "raid" + the map's "raid" overrides, docs/raid.md): mode, clock, raider types, extraction points (pos, radius, channel, open/sleep cycle, call/follow helicopters, requirements), objectives, loot tables, interactable types, how many raiders / interactables the map has, and warnings.

tools.name: raid_set
tools.description: Replace or merge the raid block (docs/raid.md): target 'rules' (default) writes rules.json "raid", target 'map' the open map's "raid" (mode, duration, startDelay, points, objectives by id). merge=true merges top-level keys; delete=true removes the block. Validated before saving (readable errors, nothing written on failure).

tools.name: raid_point
tools.description: Add / replace (by id) or delete an extraction point on the open map (its "raid".points; undoable). point = {id, pos [x, z], radius, channel, opensAt, open, sleep, arrival, departure, requires, scope player|point, contest block|ignore|reset, leave reset|pause, interruptOnDamage, capacity, call, follow, team, fn}; unspecified keys use rules raid.extraction.

tools.name: raid_run
tools.description: Run a bot raid on the open map (headless, deterministic): raiders loot, complete required objectives and extract. Returns the final phase, winner team, each player's receipt (outcome, secured / lost items, value, objectives, reward bundle, operation id) and a timeline of point phases, interactions, objectives and extractions.

tools.name: route_list
tools.description: Authored routes of the open map (map "routes"; docs/game-format.md § Routes): from / to entity ids, control points, per-point offsets, raw lines, blockers, line-0 length and AI length, plus the map "screen" block. With routes, units are only sent between garrisons that have a route.

tools.name: route_set
tools.description: Add or replace the route between two garrison entities (ids or indices; entities without an id get one). 'points' [[x, z], ...] control points from the first garrison to the second (at least 2; a point may be {"at": [x, z], "offsets": [8 numbers], "zone": int, "slowdown": n}); optional 'lines' (raw nodes per line), 'blockers' (entity ids that close the route while alive), 'flying'. Without points: a straight route (in / out points).

tools.name: route_delete
tools.description: Delete authored routes: 'from' + 'to' (either direction), or 'index', or 'all': true.

tools.name: route_generate
tools.description: Author straight routes as a starting point: for every pair of garrison entities (or those within 'maxDistance' cells) that has no route yet, a route with in / out points lanes.routes.inOut from each end. 'replace': true regenerates existing ones too. Edit the points afterwards with route_set.

tools.name: screen_set
tools.description: Set or delete the map "screen": 'size' [w, h] cells, 'center' [x, z] (default map centre), 'bounds' [left, right, top, bottom] how far scripts may move the centre, 'smooth' camera follow rate; 'delete': true removes it. Garrisons off the screen do not grow.

tools.name: road_types
tools.description: Road types for spline roads (docs/roads.md): the built-in library (city streets, avenues, boulevard, one-way, highways and ramps, rural roads, gravel / dirt roads, paths) plus rules "roadTypes". Each: id, name, category, lanes per direction (use, width in cells), median, curbs / sidewalks / barriers per side, surface, width, props.

tools.name: road_type_set
tools.description: Add or change a road type in rules "roadTypes" (metres, km/h). 'id', 'type': {"extends": "street_2", "name", "lanes": {"forward": 2 | ["car", "bus", "parking"], "backward": .., "width": 3.5}, "median": {"width", "surface", "barrier", "curb"}, "sides" / "left" / "right": {"curb": none|low|high|sloped|shoulder, "sidewalk", "shoulder", "shoulderSurface", "barrier": none|guardrail|concrete|fence|wall|hedge}, "surface", "centre": none|dashed|solid|double|yellow, "speed", "props": [{"shape": lamp|tree|bush|flowerbed|bollard|pole|bench|sign or "model" or "type", "side": -1|0|1|2, "spacing", "phase", "offset"}]}. null removes the game's type.

tools.name: road_network
tools.description: The open map's spline road network (map "roadNetwork"): nodes (id, x, z, y = metres over the ground), edges (id, a, b, type, c1 / c2 Bezier control points [x, z, height], attachA / attachB = lanes of another edge the end leaves from), per-edge length / bridges / tunnels, junctions (arms, signal) and problems.

tools.name: road_add
tools.description: Draw a road: 'points' [[x, z] or [x, z, height], ...] (2 or more; heights in metres over the ground: > 1.5 makes a bridge, < -2.5 a tunnel) or node ids; 'type' (road_types); 'curve': "straight" (a polyline, default), "smooth" (one smooth spline through the points) or "bezier" (exactly [a, c1, c2, b]). Ends snap to nodes and edges within 'snap' cells (default 1.5): a road ending on an edge splits it into a junction. 'fromLanes' {"edge": id, "lanes": [first, last], "dir": 1|-1} starts the road on those lanes of a road (a ramp / branch, the first point on that road); 'toLanes' likewise for the end (a merge). 'reversed' for one-way types.

tools.name: road_node_set
tools.description: Move a road node: 'node' id, 'x', 'z' (cells), 'y' (metres over the ground: bridges / tunnels). The control points next to it follow.

tools.name: road_edge_set
tools.description: Change a road edge: 'edge' id; 'type'; 'c1' / 'c2' ([x, z] or [x, z, height]) to bend it, 'straight': true to straighten; 'y1' / 'y2' heights of the control points; 'reversed'.

tools.name: road_stop_set
tools.description: Bus stop bay ("карман") on a road edge: the carriageway widens at the kerb, the sidewalk gives way, a shelter stands behind it. 'edge' id; 'at' (0..1 along the edge) or 'point' [x, z] (its nearest place, and the side it is on); 'side' 1 right / -1 left of a -> b; 'length' / 'taper' metres (default 18 / 12); 'width' metres (default: the kerb lane); 'shelter' (default true). 'remove': true deletes the bay nearest to 'at' / 'point'. 'parking': true makes a parking zone instead (marked spaces, 'stall' metres each, default 6; width 2.5 m, taper 5 m, length 24 m): in the parking lane where the road has one on that side, else a bay cut into the sidewalk.

tools.name: road_driveway_set
tools.description: Driveway ("заезд во двор") on a road edge: the kerb and sidewalk come down over short flares, an asphalt apron crosses the sidewalk and runs on into the yard. 'edge' id; 'at' (0..1) or 'point' [x, z] (its nearest place, and the side it is on); 'side' 1 right / -1 left of a -> b; 'width' metres (default 3.5); 'depth' metres into the yard behind the sidewalk (default 6). 'remove': true deletes the driveway nearest to 'at' / 'point'.

tools.name: road_split
tools.description: Split a road edge into two at a point ('at' [x, z]) or Bezier parameter 't' (0..1); returns the new node.

tools.name: road_delete
tools.description: Delete road edges ('edges': ids) and / or nodes with their edges ('nodes': ids); 'all': true clears the network.

tools.name: nereid_water_state
tools.description: Native NEREID surfaces and resolved authoring currents.

tools.name: nereid_flow_set
tools.description: Set NEREID manual velocity or automatic slope current; editable grade in degrees. Undoable map authoring, does not mutate legacy waterNetwork.

tools.name: water_types
tools.description: Shore types of water from splines (docs/water.md): the built-in library (embankment, embankment_stone, cliff, beach, bank) plus rules "shoreTypes" (a game retunes a type by id, gives its own textures per surface and prop models). Each: id, name, kind (embankment | cliff | beach | natural) and its sizes in metres.

tools.name: water_network
tools.description: The map's water ("waterNetwork"): bodies (strait / river: centre line [x, z, width m]; sea: map side and shore line [x, z]) with their shore segments per bank (metres along, shore type, hand-drawn or auto).

tools.name: water_set
tools.description: Adds or replaces one water body and bakes the map (cells under the water become '~', under cliffs '#'; shores "auto" are recomputed). body: {id?, kind: strait | river | sea, points: [[x, z, widthMetres], ...] (strait, river: centre line in cells, at least 2 points, smoothed) or side: north|south|east|west + shore: [[x, z], ...] (sea), depth?, shores?: "auto" | [{side, from, to, type}]}. tiles?: {water: 'w', cliff: 'x'} - chars the bake also writes into the map's tiles layer. Strait: embankments on both banks; river: embankment by the town, natural bank elsewhere; sea: embankment by the town, cliffs at headlands and map ends, beaches between.

tools.name: water_delete
tools.description: Removes a water body by id and bakes the map again (its cells get back what was there).

tools.name: water_shores
tools.description: Shore segments of one water body. Either a hand-drawn segment {id, side (-1 left / 1 right bank of a strait / river, 1 for the sea), from, to (metres along the bank), type (water_types)}: kept over auto; or {id, reset: true}: drop the hand-drawn ones (all auto again). Bakes the map.

tools.name: water_bake
tools.description: Bakes the map's water again (after the roads, the rules or the map changed): cells, auto shores, and a check that the land is one piece (spline road bridges join parts).

tools.name: game_make_options
tools.description: The game wizard ("Сделать игру"): what can be chosen for game_make — templates with their mechanics and orientation, features, tutorial modes, map presets and sizes, stores, platforms, languages, and the default answers.

tools.name: game_make_plan
tools.description: What game_make would make for these answers, without writing files: the template and why (from the idea's words, the features, the orientation; the seed breaks ties), the tutorial shape (economy / garrison / generic), the level generator, meta parts.

title.description: game title (also the project folder and the .aiverse name)

artDir.description: folder with art, models, music, sounds, fonts and .md/.txt texts (a GDD is read as the idea)

artUrl.description: link to an image / archive (.zip, .tar.gz) with the content; downloaded with curl

idea.description: what the game is about, any language; empty = the wizard decides

metaIdea.description: wishes for the meta game (menus, progression, shop, events), passed to the agent step

features.description: wanted mechanics: economy base army garrison lanes waves territory heroes spells survival planets 2d casual portrait

tutorial.description: hard = a step-by-step tutorial map, soft = one-time hints in matches

mapPreset.description: map generator preset for levels, 'auto' or 'none' (copies of the base map)

verifyLevels.description: bot matches on the tutorial and a sample of levels

seed.description: 0 = from the title and the idea

ai.description: the game's own texts per language (an agent writes it): {tagline, intro: {lang: text}, types / resources / currencies / upgrades: {id: {lang: text}}, levels: [{lang: text}]}

tools.name: game_make
tools.description: Make a whole game project from a few answers and open it: a template picked by the idea, the user's art / models / music / sounds / fonts from artDir or artUrl (models and sprites on the types they are named after, music by name into playlists, the key art into the splash, an icon, UI colours), a step-by-step hard tutorial map built from the rules (only the needed commands pass, the enemy waits), one-time hints in matches, generated levels with stars and rewards, the meta screens (home, levels, upgrades that buff the match, shop, daily reward, profile, settings, result), purchases / ads when asked, language files, a check with bots, WIZARD.md and the .aiverse. Takes up to a minute (bot checks); verifyLevels false is faster.

artDir.description: folder with art, models, music, sounds, fonts and .md/.txt texts (a GDD is read as the idea)

ai.description: the game's own texts per language (an agent writes it): {tagline, intro: {lang: text}, types / resources / currencies / upgrades: {id: {lang: text}}, levels: [{lang: text}]}

tools.name: lightbake_get
tools.description: Baked lighting of the open map: its bake settings (the map's 'bake' block over the defaults) and what the bake folder maps/<map>.bake holds (hash, mode, stats: regions, pages, texels, probes). Modes: indirect (lightmap = indirect light, sun realtime), shadowmask (+ baked sun shadows for far / shadowless views, default), subtractive (sun baked too, cheapest on phones).

tools.name: lightbake_set
tools.description: Change the open map's bake settings (stored in the map's 'bake' block; save the map to keep them). Keys: quality (preview | medium | high preset), mode (indirect | shadowmask | subtractive), texelsPerUnit, pageSize, samples, bounces, aoDistance, aoStrength, denoise, indirectIntensity, maskSamples, probeSpacing, probeHeight, probeSamples, padding. Then lightbake_bake (needs the editor).

tools.name: lightbake_clear
tools.description: Delete the open map's baked lighting (the folder maps/<map>.bake): the game falls back to realtime lighting. Generated lightmap UVs next to models (*.lmuv) are kept.

tools.name: human_schema
tools.description: VIVID digital-human authoring schema (the Studio 'Human Creator' window): sections skin, eyes, groom (hair), anatomy (face and body proportions), expression (52 ARKit-order rest channels), routes (channel -> morph target, gain 0..4), rig (bone names), rigCorrections and skinWeights. Each field has key (DNA path for human_edit 'set'), kind, min/max. Also presets, channel names and the reference human's rig nodes / morph targets / vertex count.

tools.name: human_list
tools.description: Saved digital humans of the open game (humans/<name>.json).

tools.name: human_get
tools.description: One saved digital human: its full document (dna, rigCorrections, skinWeights, routes) and the rig node / morph target names of the generated reference human.

tools.name: human_create
tools.description: Create humans/<name>.json from a preset (neutral | warm | cool | stylized; default neutral). Fails if it exists unless overwrite:true. Edit it with human_edit; open it in Studio > Human Creator > Load to see it.

tools.name: human_edit
tools.description: Edit a saved digital human in one all-or-nothing transaction (nothing is written if any edit is invalid), applied in this order: preset (resets the DNA), set {key: value} with keys from human_schema (e.g. 'skin.melanin': 0.6, 'eyes.irisColor': [0.2,0.4,0.3], 'groom.lengthMeters': 0.3, 'anatomy.jawWidth': 1.1, 'expressionRest.24': 0.4, 'rig.headBone': 'head'), routes (REPLACES the list: [{channel, target, gain}]), rig ([{node, translation:[x,y,z]}], |x|,|y|,|z| <= 1, [0,0,0] removes), skin ([{vertex, joint, weight}] or [{vertex, erase:true}]).

set.description: DNA path -> value (number, [r,g,b] colour, string bone, string[] optionalBones)

tools.name: human_look_schema
tools.description: Character Creator look fields for an imported character model (Studio > Character Creator: Skin, Eyes, Hair, Body): key, label, min, max, initial. A look is {version:1, values:{key:number}, materials:{sourceMaterial: role}}.

tools.name: human_look_list
tools.description: Saved Character Creator looks of the open game (human-looks/<name>.json); Studio shows them as preset cards.

tools.name: human_look_get
tools.description: One saved Character Creator look with every value (defaults filled in).

tools.name: human_look_save
tools.description: Write a Character Creator look (agent draft from a text description). 'values' {key: number} from human_look_schema are merged onto 'base' (another saved look) or the defaults; 'materials' maps source material -> role. Fails if the look exists unless overwrite:true. The artist then applies it in Studio > Character Creator > Presets.

tools.name: human_metahuman_check
tools.description: MetaHuman compatibility adapter (no Unreal at runtime): inspect a permitted MetaHuman export in the open game (content-relative glTF/GLB/FBX path) and return detection, head bone, face meshes, material roles for the Character Creator look, ARKit channel coverage vs VIVID's 52, FACIAL/corrective joint counts, LOD levels and plain notes on unsupported parts (RigLogic correctives, strand groom). save_look:<name> also writes human-looks/<name>.json with those roles.

tools.name: studio_character_snapshot
tools.description: PNG of the character shown in the open Studio's Character Creator viewport (Studio must run with this game and the character shown). view: face | torso | full (default face). Returns the PNG path; open it to SEE your edit before reporting. Waits up to 15 s.

tools.name: human_validate
tools.description: Check a digital-human document (as written by hand) without saving: version 1, dna limits, rig corrections, skin weights, routes. Returns ok or the first error.

tools.name: graph_catalog
tools.description: Discover actual registered graph domain operations, payload formats and save constraints.

tools.name: graph_list
tools.description: List native assets in one graph domain.

tools.name: graph_get
tools.description: Read native graph or model document with owner metadata.

tools.name: graph_node_catalog
tools.description: Read the native node/authoring catalog when provided by the owner.

tools.name: graph_validate
tools.description: Validate a candidate using the native domain compiler. No write.

tools.name: graph_diagnostics
tools.description: Run native validation and return domain diagnostics; not runtime telemetry.

tools.name: graph_dependencies
tools.description: List explicit schema references from a candidate. No filesystem writes or runtime inference.

tools.name: graph_property_schema
tools.description: Describe supported typed node properties; SpectraFX returns native catalog defaults, not inferred constraints.

tools.name: graph_asset_dependencies
tools.description: Inspect literal asset references and embedded animation subgraph recursion; no writes.

tools.name: graph_live_snapshot
tools.description: Read actual native editor owner telemetry if the owner is registered; never starts or modifies play.

tools.name: graph_live_watch
tools.description: Start, inspect or stop native owner telemetry subscription. No gameplay mutation.

tools.name: graph_live_profile
tools.description: Opt-in native common MotionWeave instance CPU profiling. No GPU timings or gameplay controls.

tools.name: texture_graph_gpu_preview
tools.description: Queue/read native Metal or Vulkan texture preview, single bake or full PBR set; publish completed bake explicitly.

materialized.description: Opt-in experimental native materialized DAG execution

incremental.description: Opt-in dedicated materialized pass slots and exact-source reuse; supports pointwise fusion; requires native device lease

fusePointwise.description: Opt-in bounded pointwise fusion for materialized DAG; also supported in plan inspection

gpuTextureTransfer.description: Experimental GPU-resident full materialized set; actual copied mip zero is CPU-reference validated; requires native lease

incrementalOutputs.description: Direct fence-only incremental material set for exact live target; reuse immutable previously published outputs; not supported by queue or plan

gpuTextureFenceOnly.description: Explicit material-only GPU completion without CPU pixel validation or PNG export; requires gpuTextureTransfer

gpuTextureMipmaps.description: Generate full GPU mip chain for copied textures; requires gpuTextureTransfer

tools.name: graph_gpu_profile
tools.description: Opt-in completed native RHI scope timing capture; optional Texture Graph region detail (not per-fused-node timing).

textureGroupDetail.description: On start, replace materialized aggregate dispatch timing with per-region and output-pack scopes

tools.name: graph_runtime_capabilities
tools.description: Discover isolated CPU probes and unavailable live telemetry. No GPU measurements.

tools.name: graph_debug_session
tools.description: Control one isolated CPU debug instance. Explicit bounded advancement; no live game controls.

tools.name: graph_runtime_probe
tools.description: Execute a bounded isolated native CPU preview. Not live game telemetry.

tools.name: graph_edit
tools.description: Apply 1..64 native-schema draft edits atomically in memory. Returns candidate and native diagnostics; never saves.

tools.name: graph_save
tools.description: Explicit native save; respects domain revision contracts. No apply, bake or runtime execution.

tools.name: battle_net_simulate
tools.description: Network check of direct-control battles (hosted battle server + secure UDP + rollback) on a simulated mobile link: bot players in a reference top-down duel, all on a virtual clock. 'profile' lan|wifi|4g|3g|bad (bad = 20% loss, 150 ms RTT, jitter), overrides loss / rttMs / jitterMs; matches, players, seconds, tickRate; optional inputDelay / rollbackWindow / lagToleranceMs (default: the engine's mobile battle settings); 'suspend' backgrounds one phone for 6 s, 'rebind' changes another's address. Reports finished matches, agreed results, desyncs, rollbacks, how far clients run ahead, server cost and bytes per player. Nothing is saved.

tools.name: fx_asset_check
tools.description: Check an indexed model or texture GUID using native Studio CPU decoding; does not verify GPU upload.

tools.name: fx_replay_prepare
tools.description: Prepare a native SpectraFX replay at an exact tick with optional CPU RNG seed, Metal allocation seed or Metal shader seed. Poll fx_replay_status until replayReady.

tools.name: fx_checkpoint_file
tools.description: Transfer SPFT checkpoint in ordered 32 KiB hex chunks; import runs on render owner.

tools.name: fx_checkpoint_timeline
tools.description: Save or restore a paused Metal preview checkpoint; poll fx_replay_status for completion.

tools.name: fx_replay_status
tools.description: Read native SpectraFX replay readiness, tick, GPU seed retry state and backend. Requires a running Studio FX viewport.

tools.name: fx_replay_capture
tools.description: Queue or poll a bounded native SpectraFX JPEG capture. Use action=capture with requireReplayReady=true; then action=captureStatus. Provenance is request-time, not exact GPU frame completion.
